summary: We developed Loop the Difference, an interactive sky-investigation tool that turns NASA SPHEREx observations into a search for what moves and changes in the infrared sky. A user enters a name or RA/Dec. The app queries every SPHEREx release at NASA/IPAC IRSA, cuts out the same patch at each visit, aligns the images on one grid and blinks two comparable epochs, the technique that revealed Pluto in 1930. Behind the blink, a pipeline registers B onto A on field stars, matches their flux and PSFs, and computes a ZOGY significance image, so real changes stand out from noise. Every detected source is cross-matched with ESA Gaia DR3, moved to each frame's date, and with AllWISE. Unmatched sources are flagged for verification. Users can mark a candidate in two frames, see its possible track, look back at older SPHEREx visits, WISE and 1950s photographic plates, and check known asteroids with SkyBoT and NASA JPL. A 102-band quick-look spectrum reads molecular bands like methane and water ice, and a UMAP source map ranks unusual objects first. Every result carries its quality checks and provenance. Loop the Difference is a discovery aid, never a discovery claim.
details:
Loop the Difference is an interactive web tool that turns NASA SPHEREx observations into a search for what moves and changes in the sky. A user types an object name or coordinates. The app queries every SPHEREx release at NASA/IPAC IRSA, cuts out the same patch of sky at each visit, aligns all images on one grid and blinks two comparable epochs, the technique that revealed Pluto in 1930. Behind the blink, a pipeline registers the images on field stars, matches their brightness and sharpness, and computes a ZOGY significance image, so rise.

Unmatched sources are flagged for verification. Users can see its possibletrack and look back at older SPHEREx visits, WISE and archival photographic plates. They can also choT and NASA JPL. A102-band quick-look spectrum reads molecular bands such as water ice and methane, and a UMAP sour objects first.

We built it with Python for the backend and React, TypeScript and Aladin Lite for the interface. It runs in Docker on a Google Cloud.

The project is creative human method with a modern spectral survey and machine-learning ranking. Students, amateurs and researchers can explore the app.

We paid close attention on quality checks (overlap, sharpness, noise) and the provenance of its data.
